Yield curve moves

Steepening or flattening is the change in long minus short. Bull: yields fell on average; bear: they rose. Moves under 5 bp count as unchanged.

Data as of the latest close; it may be delayed, revised or incomplete and is provided without warranty of any kind. Past levels and relationships do not predict future results. Third-party index, spread and options data remain the property of their respective owners; no endorsement by any data provider is implied. Treasury yields: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15). Financial stress indexes: Federal Reserve Banks of Chicago and St. Louis. Retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Index levels are price indexes. Credit spreads are option-adjusted spreads over Treasuries, except Baa and Aaa corporate, which are yields minus the 10Y Treasury. The option-adjusted spread series start in November 2023, so their percentiles cover that history only. A value marked * is carried forward from the last print. 1Y, 3Y and 5Y rank against that many trading days up to the date; Lifetime ranks against all history up to the date; Full sample ranks against all history including later dates, so it uses hindsight. "1M chg pct" ranks the 21-day change against all 21-day changes in the window. Inverted call skew: share of the 100 largest S&P 500 members whose 1-month 25-delta call implied vol is above at-the-money.
